title: CPV hosts have small transverse speed residuals in 4,091 TESS rapid rotators, but extra age evidence depends on model choice
abstract: We test whether motion gives age evidence beyond luminosity for complex periodic variables (CPVs). We use published Gaia DR3 values and labels for 4,091 TESS rapid rotators from sectors 56 to 107. Relative to a common motion fit to other stars at height >1 mag above the main sequence, the median transverse residual is 2.23 km/s for 126 CPV hosts and 6.23 km/s for 3,965 other stars. At height >2 mag, the medians are 2.01 and 2.25 km/s. A logistic model adjusted for height, period and color gives an odds ratio of 0.67 (95% interval 0.44 to 1.01) per doubling of 1 + residual/(5 km/s). Adding detection and sky variables gives 0.52 (0.31 to 0.87). The one-sector subset gives 1.05 (0.51 to 2.17). The direction is stable when one sky block is removed, but the extra evidence depends on model and subset choice. The motions agree with youth. They do not give an independent age scale or material lifetime. Source selection, shared groups, missing radial velocities, uncertain labels and no error propagation limit inference. New code, aggregate results, synthetic checks, input hashes and separate-scratch repeat steps are included. External records are excluded.

display.caption: Velocity residuals by height and conditional model intervals. Much of the raw contrast follows luminosity. Null-compatible subset results do not establish no association.
